cards.back: Dividing the network to limit lateral movement after a compromise.
Disabling unnecessary services, patching, applying a secure baseline, and removing default accounts.
Running a suspicious file in an isolated environment to observe its behavior safely.
Decoy system that attracts attackers and logs their techniques.
Entire network of decoys to study lateral movement and reconnaissance.
Honeyfile = decoy file; honeytoken = fake credential or token. Any use is a hostile signal.
Non-existent but plausible account: any login attempt reveals the attacker.
NIDS = out-of-band network detection; NIPS = inline network prevention that blocks.
HIDS = host agent that alerts on files/logs; HIPS = host agent that blocks behaviors.
Wireless IPS: detects and blocks rogue access points and Wi-Fi attacks.
Web Application Firewall: filters HTTP traffic at the application layer (SQLi, XSS).
Unified Threat Management: single appliance combining firewall, IPS, antivirus, filtering, and VPN.
Layer 4 = IP/port/protocol; Layer 7 = application content (HTTP, payload).
Limits the number of requests per time period to counter abuse and floods.
Endpoint Detection and Response: agent that detects behaviors and can isolate the host. It is NOT a firewall.
Extended Detection and Response: correlates endpoint, network, cloud, and identity.
Data Loss Prevention: identifies and blocks sensitive data based on content rules, on the agent or network.
SPF = authorized servers; DKIM = signature; DMARC = alignment policy; BIMI = verified logo.
Secrets scanning = detecting keys and passwords in code; code signing = signing binaries to prove origin and integrity.
802.1X authenticates at the network port; endpoint posture checks patches/antivirus before granting access.
